items.html: (To the question) Because there is no coupling in the hairs of the beard, except at the time of the ascent of the GAR of AA to Atik, from where the hairs of the beard were drawn, namely, from the Mochin of AA at the time of their emergence in the Reisha de Lo It Yeda; and then Aba and Ima are included in AA, and AA in the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, and the coupling is made in the aspect of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, as is known. Behold, the matter of the inclusion of Aba and Ima in the Mazal draws them to the aspect of Atik. (Item 95. Part 1, Page 552, s.v. "and therefore").

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 208:1
items.html: It was explained above in Answer 176, the great difference between the Hochma of the thirty-two paths and the Hochma of AA: the Hochma of AA is the Hochma of the direct light, and is bestowed through the mouth of the upper one, in the manner of the coming out of the Partzufim of AK. However, the Hochma of the thirty-two paths is bestowed only through the coupling of the Yesods, because it has no root at all in the GAR of any Partzuf, but only in its NHY; and therefore this Hochma is discerned as coming from below upward, from ZA to Bina. In the secret of the verse, "Fair in elevation," and "forest," with MTzL, as above in Part 12, that the Mem, which is Hochma, bestows to the Tzadi, which is ZA, and from the Tzadi the Hochma rises and is bestowed to the Lamed, which is Bina, see there. It was also explained above in Answer 200, that the hairs of the beard are discerned only as the AHP of the hairs of the head, which are the aspect of ZON and the aspect of NHY, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 208:2
items.html: And it is found that "just as the Mocha Stima'ah sealed its bone, so that it would not be revealed except through the hairs, so Aba sealed the bone, so that it would not be revealed except through its clothing." Meaning, just as the principal revelation of this Hochma in the place of its emergence in AA is not from the aspect of the Mocha Stima'ah, which is the Hochma of the direct light, but only through the MAN of the hairs, which are the aspect of the NHY, and ZON, where the Mazal VeNotzer is the Tifferet and the Mazal VeNakeh is the Yesod; so Aba and Ima of the stature of AB, called Aba, also sealed this Hochma, so that it would not be bestowed below, except through clothing in his Yesod. In this manner there are here two sealings: one is that of the Mazal VeNakeh, which is the Yesod of the beard, because of which the Hochma of the direct light of the Mocha Stima'ah itself was diminished to the aspect of the Hochma of the thirty-two paths, which are bestowed from the NHY to the GAR, and their entire essence is nothing but the Tifferet, which is the entire bearer of this Hochma, as above in Answer 176. Behold, this is a very great diminution. And nevertheless the Tifferet is discerned here as illuminating without a sheath, but in the entire measure of its perfection, in the utmost revelation, because the aspect of the Mazal VeNakeh, which is the Yesod, stands here from below upward, and the Tifferet, which is VeNotzer, is not covered at all by it. And this is only for Aba and Ima, which receive the Mochin in the place of their emergence.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 208:3
items.html: However, there is a second sealing, which is "that also Aba sealed this Hochma, so that it would not be revealed, except through clothing in his Yesod," which is the secret of the clothing of the sun in its sheath. For because the Mochin are not bestowed from Aba and Ima downward, except through his Yesod, which is included of male and female, which are Joseph and Benjamin, it is found that the screen in the Yesod is made into the aspect of an Emanator of this Hochma, and this causes that the Tifferet does not illuminate in its own measure, in revelation, but from within the measure of the Yesod; and a great limitation is made for the measure of the Tifferet, and because of this it acquired the name "crown of Hesed," for it does not illuminate but as the measure of the crown of the Yesod, which is the aspect of the screen in it.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 208:4
items.html: (To the question) And we have already elaborated on this in the previous answers, and remember well these two sealings, for without them there is no true understanding of the Mochin of AB. (Item 99).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 209:1
items.html: (To the question) You already know that the two Mazalot are the aspects of the five Hassadim and the five Gevurot, which are called the brain of Daat. For the Mazal VeNotzer is the Tifferet and the five Hassadim, and the Mazal VeNakeh is the Yesod and the five Gevurot. And this brain of Daat is discerned as included for Aba and Ima, meaning that the Hochma that came out in Aba and Ima came only by virtue of it, for it is what couples them face-to-face, and it is the first receiver of the Hochma, and is considered its root, as is said above in the secret of the verse, "forest," with MTzL. (Item 102).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 210:1
items.html: (To the question) The inclusion of Aba and Ima in the Mazal is in two aspects: one, when the hairs of the beard are in the aspect of Makifim alone, and they clothe the HGT of AA, and are only the stature of SAG; then Aba and Ima are discerned as VAK of AB, because they have no grip in the head of AA, which is the GAR of AB, but only in the body. The second is at the time that they rise to the GAR of AA, and the hairs enter into the internality of the vessels in the secret of MAN, when they attain the GAR of the lights of AB and the NHY of the vessels. Behold, Aba and Ima are sometimes lacking a head, although they are included in the Mazal, namely, at the time that they are only Makifim alone. (Item 105).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 211:1
items.html: (To the question) Because they attain the aspect of the smallness of AB from the hairs of the head and the beard, while they are in the secret of Makifim upon them. (Item 105).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 212:1
items.html: It is known that at the time of the coupling of the mouth of AA, to bring out the stature of AB, the GAR of AA rose to the GAR of Atik, and the mouth of AA is found in the place of the mouth of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda. And the throat, with the HGT of AA, rose and became his KHB, and with them also Aba and Ima rose and clothe these new KHB. And since the throat and HGT rose to the place of the previous GAR of AA, the throat, with the four lower corrections hanging from it, now stands in the place of the Galgalta of AA; and then the four lower corrections entered into the internality of the vessels, in the secret of the MAN in the throat, which are the aspect of the Alef, He, Het, Ayin, and rose to the MAN in the palate, which is in the mouth of AA, standing near them in the place of the mouth of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, where also entered the aspect of the eight upper corrections hanging at the end of the cheeks of the head, and they came into the internality of the vessels, in the secret of the MAN in the palate, which is the secret of the Gime, Yod, Kaf, Kuf. And it is found that the palate, which stands in the mouth of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, and the throat, which stands in the place of the Galgalta of AA of before, couple with one another, in the secret of the coupling of the palate and throat of AA; and the eight upper corrections are found to join with the four lower corrections, through this coupling.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 212:2
items.html: (To the question) Behold, through the ascent of AA to the GAR of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, it was corrected that "the four lower corrections became the aspect of MAN and joined with the eight upper corrections in the palate of AA," for they too entered, from the place of the end of the cheeks of the head, into the internality of the vessels, which is the palate of AA. And in the secret of the bowing of the head of AA, from the place of ascent to its previous place, this coupling comes out in the palate and throat of AA, in the previous place, where now also the mouth of Aba and Ima is found; and then Aba and Ima receive the aspect of the eight corrections in the palate of AA, which are the aspect of the Gime, Yod, Kaf, Kuf, with the four lower corrections in the throat of AA, which are the aspect of the Alef, He, Het, Ayin, and they were made there into the aspect of MAN and into the aspect of the Daat of Aba and Ima, serving them from below upward. And the stature of AB comes out in the place of the head of Aba and Ima. And understand well. (Item 105).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 213:1
items.html: (To the question) ZON, which rise as MAN to Aba and Ima, at the time that they feel the lack of the illumination of Hochma, through the raising of the MAN of the souls of the righteous to them, cause also in the upper Ima the need for the illumination of Hochma, in order to bestow to ZON, by virtue of their being her children, namely, by virtue of the connection that Bina has with ZON, from the secret of the ten Sefirot of the direct light, where Bina bestows there the illumination of Hochma to ZON. And therefore also Aba and Ima rise to the GAR of AA and are included in the coupling of AA, palate and throat, in the secret of the Mazalot, as above in Answer 212. (Items 103 and 104).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 214:1
items.html: (To the question) At the time of the coupling, the mouth and head of AA stand in the place of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, as is known, and it was explained above in Answer 212, that for the need of Aba and Ima, AA bows his head downward, to the place of his previous GAR, where Aba and Ima stand. Behold, the head of AA descended below the end of his mouth, for his mouth is in the place of the mouth of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, and his head descended to the place of the previous head, which is below the end of the mouth; and then it is also found that the throat and HGT, which rose to the place of the previous head of AA, are now found, at the time of the bowing of the head of AA downward, that the throat is included in the head of AA itself, because it descended to the place of the standing of the throat and HGT. As all this is said above in Answer 212. See there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 215:1
items.html: (To the question) At the time of the ascent of the HGT of AA to his GAR, only the two upper thirds of each one of the HGT rose to the GAR of AA and became the aspect of the heads of Aba and Ima. However, the lower thirds of each one of the HGT did not rise there, and remained as the aspect of the body for Aba and Ima, as is known. And behold, all their part in the Tifferet of AA is only the upper third. And it is now found, at the time of the ascent, that that upper third is divided into three thirds: the two upper thirds of this third rose to the GAR of AA, and the lower third of this third remained as the aspect of the body for Aba and Ima. Behold, only a ninth part of the Tifferet of AA remained as the aspect of the body for Aba and Ima, for even when they were in the HGT, they had only a third of the Tifferet, and afterwards, when two thirds of it rose to the head, only a third of a third remained, which is a ninth. (Item 107).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 216:1
items.html: (To the question) Because the throat and HGT of AA rise at the time of the coupling and become the KHB of AA, namely, they rise to his GAR; behold, it is found that the four lower corrections, which were hanging on the throat of AA, now rose to the place of the Galgalta of AA, and were included in the head of AA. (Item 107).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 217:1
items.html: (To the question) Because he himself has the AB of the direct light, and he has no need at all for the AB of the Mazalot, which are a very low aspect in relation to the Hochma of the direct light. (Item 108).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 218:1
items.html: (To the question) It is the aspect of the VAK of AB, which Aba and Ima receive from the Mazalot and the hairs of the head, while they are still upon them as Makifim. (Item 108).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 219:1
items.html: (To the question) The Mochin of AB of the thirty-two paths, in their entirety, are divided into three aspects of MALZ: the aspect of the Mem is in the Mochin in the place of their emergence, in the GAR of AA; and the aspect of the Lamed is after they were clothed in the Yesods of Aba and Ima, and came to the place of the throat and HGT of AA, where Aba and Ima clothe from the aspect of permanence; and the aspect of the Tzadi is after their clothing in the Mochin of ZA. And they are explained according to the order of the six aspects, see above in Answer 42. And behold, in exactly this manner are also divided the hairs of AA and the hairs of ZA: the aspect of the eight upper corrections of the beard are the aspect of the Mem of the hairs, and the four lower corrections, hanging on the throat and HGT, are the Lamed of the hairs, and the hairs of the NHY, which are the lower beard, are the Tzadi of the hairs. And therefore, at first, namely, at thirteen years and one day, and likewise in the Mochin of weekdays, ZA receives only the aspect of the Tzadi of the hairs, which is the lower beard, because then he receives only from the NHY of these Mochin, namely, from the NHY of Aba and Ima. And on the Sabbath, at Musaf, when ZA rises and clothes the place of Aba and Ima on the HGT of AA, he then attains the Lamed of the hairs; and at Mincha, when he rises to the place of the GAR of AA, he then attains the Mem of the hairs, and his beard is filled with all the thirteen corrections, like AA. Behold, at the time that he rises only to the NHY of Aba and Ima, he has only the lower beard alone, which is the Tzadi, as explained. (Item 110).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 220:1
items.html: (To the question) Because the matter of the ascent of the hands of AA to the aspect of his GAR raises Aba and Ima to receive the stature of AB, which is Hochma; and since the upper aspect is Hochma, there is no need here to consider the aspect of Bina in the middle joints of the hands, because they do not rise then under that name, but are included in the upper aspect, which is Hochma. And therefore he considers only the upper joints of the hands, which became the Hochmas of Aba and Ima: Aba attained the stature of AB from the aspect of the right hand, and Ima attained the stature of AB from the aspect of the left hand, and this alone is what needs to be announced to us. (Item 112).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 221:1
items.html: (To the question) The root of the Mochin of AB of the thirty-two paths are the HGT of AA, which rose to his GAR; through the bowing of the head, in the place of these HGT that rose, the stature of AB came out upon the MAN of the Mazalot, as is known. And therefore these HGT were then divided into two aspects: head and body. For the two upper thirds became the head, and the lower third of each one became the body. And it is discerned that the aspect of the two upper thirds of each one, which became the head, are the inheritance of Aba and Ima, in which ZON have no part, but receive them from the aspect of the coupling of Aba and Ima. And the aspect of the lower thirds, which are the aspect of the body, are the aspect of the inheritance of ZA, for through the ascent of the NHY of AA to his HGT, ZA is found included in these lower thirds that remained in the HGT, called the heads of the shoulders of AA; and therefore they are considered the share of ZA himself, for he is included in them literally, at the time of the coupling. Behold, the two shoulders of AA are the share of ZA. (Item 113).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 222:1
items.html: (To the question) Because the Mochin of AB did not come out in the place of the two shoulders of AA, for there is no coupling except in the aspect of the head, and they came out in the place of the GAR of AA, where Aba and Ima stand and are included; and therefore, after Aba and Ima inherited their stature from his GAR, they then bestow the Mochin to ZA, in the way of the clothing of their Yesods, as is known. And all the superiority in the two crowns that ZA inherited is only on the aspect of the inclusion of ZA in them, and therefore he receives from their essentiality. For in the two upper thirds of each one of the HGT of AA, Aba and Ima were included, and in the lower thirds, ZA was included, and therefore they were divided so. However, the Mochin do not come out in the place of the heads of the shoulders of AA, but only in the place of the two upper thirds. And therefore ZA is compelled to receive them, through the clothing of the Yesods of Aba and Ima, through which they are diminished in the second sealing, as above in Answer 208. See there. (Item 115).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 223:1
items.html: (To the question) Because in the aspect of the two crowns in their place, in the heads of the shoulders of AA, there is no coupling of these Mochin at all, but they receive from the aspect of the two upper crowns in Aba and Ima, which are in their Daat. And therefore, if ZA received from the aspect of the two crowns in the place of their emergence, in the coupling of the head, where the crown of Hesed illuminates in revelation, outside the sheath, then the two crowns would illuminate in ZA more than his Hochma and Bina, because he received them in the aspect of his inclusion in them, in their essentiality, as above in Answers 221 and 222. However, since he did not receive the two crowns as they are, in the place of their emergence, but only in the way of the clothing of the Yesods of Aba and Ima, when the measure of the Tifferet is diminished, and it does not illuminate but as the measure of the crown of the Yesod, in the secret of the sun in its sheath; now they do not have such importance that they should illuminate in him more than his Hochma and Bina, although he does not receive them except through the coupling of Aba and Ima, and not in the aspect of inclusion, as in the two crowns. Nevertheless, the Mochin of Hochma and Bina in him are discerned as the principle, being upper roots of the two crowns. (Item 115).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 224:1
items.html: (To the question) See below, Answer 225.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 225:1
items.html: (To the question) It is known, the great difference between the two upper joints of the HGT, which rose to the head of AA, and in them the coupling of these Mochin of AB was made, and therefore the Tifferet illuminates in them in complete revelation, without any sheath, and they are discerned as the inheritance of Aba and Ima, for AA does not need these Mochin, and Aba and Ima inherited them. Not so the heads of the shoulders of AA, in which ZA is included at the time of his pregnancy: they need to receive the Mochin of Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura from the clothing of the Yesods of Aba and Ima, in which the Tifferet does not illuminate from its own aspect, but as the measure of the Yesod, whose meaning is only in the aspect of a passage through which to pass in it, and not in permanence and continuation. However, one must understand that the intention is not to the aspect of the Tifferet alone, but to the Mochin of Hochma, whose bearer it is, and they were diminished because of its clothing in the sheath. And therefore all four Mochin, drawn through the Yesods of Aba and Ima, are discerned by the name of drops alone, whose meaning is that the upper aspect of the Mochin, which is Hochma, was diminished, because of the clothing of the Tifferet in the sheath of the crown of the Yesod, to drops alone; for the Hochma does not illuminate but in the aspect of a passage through which to pass in it, whose measure of that Hochma is measured like a drop, namely, without continuation. And it is like the discernment of a stream of water that flows from its source and passes through it, without any cessation, versus the aspect of a drop that is cut off from the jet immediately with its appearance. And with this likeness is measured the measure of the difference between the Tifferet when it illuminates in the place of the emergence of the Mochin, in Aba and Ima, where it illuminates there in the aspect of the river that comes out of Eden, which is included in the aspect of Eden, versus the aspect of the Mochin, after their clothing in the Yesods of Aba and Ima, which illuminate there only in the aspect of a passage through which to pass in it, and there is no continuation of illumination in them. And with this you will understand well, that this matter of diminution does not touch the aspect of the Tifferet alone, but the matter is about the stature of Hochma. And this is what the Rav says, that ZA receives from Hochma and Bina the aspect of the drop, drawn from their inheritance. However, this drop includes all four Mochin — Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura — which comes first to the NHY of Aba and Ima themselves, and from there ZA, which is included in the two shoulders of AA, receives them; only that the Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura that ZA receives from the inheritance of Aba and Ima are included in the two shoulders of AA, because they were included in the essentiality of ZA, as he was attached to them at the time of the pregnancy, so that ZA has Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura from the aspect of the inheritance of Aba and Ima, and he has Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura from the aspect of the heads of the shoulders of AA. (Items 114 and 115).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 226:1
items.html: (To the question) One is the Tifferet when it is by itself, outside the sheath of the crown of the Yesod, which is only in the Mochin in the place of their emergence, in the GAR of AA. The second is when it illuminates in the measure of the crown of the Yesod, when it illuminates in the aspect of a drop, and the Tifferet is also called by the name crown, namely, the crown of Hesed, as is known. See above, in the adjacent answer. (Item 81).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 227:1
items.html: (To the question) Because the Tifferet does not illuminate in its own measure, but in the measure of the crown of the Yesod, which is the crown of Gevura. See above, in Answers 225 and 226.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 228:1
items.html: (To the question) ZA does not receive the Mochin of AB in the place of their emergence, in the GAR of AA, but receives them through the clothing in the Yesod of Aba, namely, the Aba and Ima of AB, called Aba. And the difference between them is great, as above in Answer 225. (Item 95).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 229:1
items.html: (To the question) Because there is no absence in the spiritual, and the matter of a change of place in the spiritual means a matter of addition upon its first place. (Item 124).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 230:1
items.html: (To the question) The matter of the two shoulders that ZA takes from AA, from the aspect of their essentiality itself: the intention is not that the heads of the shoulders themselves descended to ZA, for this is entirely impossible, that the aspect of the HGT should descend and become NHY, because ZA clothes only the NHY of AA, as is known. Rather, the intention is only from the aspect of inclusion, because at the time of the pregnancy, AA raises his NHY, with ZA, to his HGT; behold, ZA is then found included in the lower thirds of the Hesed and Gevura of AA, which remained in the aspect of the HGT at the time of the ascent; and since he is included in them, therefore he takes them from the aspect of their essentiality. Indeed, this is only an illumination, which descends with him to his place, in the NHY of AA. However, the aspect of the HGT of AA — the intention is to the aspect of the Lamed of the Tzelem, which he attains only at Musaf of the Sabbath. And now, in the Mochin of thirteen years, he has only the Tzadi of the Tzelem, and the Mem-Lamed remain for him in the aspect of Makifim. (Item 126).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 231:1
items.html: (To the question) These Makifim of the six aspects of the Mochin of ZA are not literally Makifim, but they are a product of the inner Mochin, for through the coupling of the Yesod in the inner Mochin with its upper Makif, the inner Mochin flash, and a part of them comes out to the outside, upon the forehead, and they become there Makifim upon the aspect of the face, which is from the forehead and below, and not upon the Mochin themselves, because they are a product of the Daat of the Mochin, which is clothed in the place of the forehead. (Item 127).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 232:1
items.html: (To the question) Because, since ZA receives the Mochin from the Yesod of Ima, the Tifferet is found, which does not illuminate in its own aspect, but as the measure of the crown of the Yesod, as above in Answer 225. And therefore the Tifferet was limited, and is called a crown, like the Gevura, and therefore both of them were made into one Mochin, for they illuminate in one measure. (Item 134).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 233:1
items.html: (To the question) It was already explained in the previous parts, that three partners always operate in the emanation of ZA, which are: AA, Aba, and Ima; and the reason was explained there, because so it came out in its root in the Nekudim, that the NHY of the inner AK, which is the Partzuf of the Keter of AK, bestowed the Vav and the point to the mouth of Aba and Ima of the Nekudim, and from there the ZAT of the Nekudim, which are the root of ZON, were born. Behold, his MAN needs to be included from the NHY of the Keter, and therefore also in Atzilut ZA does not come out except from AA, who is the Keter of Atzilut, namely, at the time of his ascent to the GAR of Atik; and there, in the GAR of Atik, the coupling is made for the need of the Mochin of ZA, namely, in his share that is drawn from the aspect of the Keter; and afterwards, through the bowing of the head of AA to the place of Aba and Ima, the Mochin are also clothed in the coupling of Aba and Ima; and then there are three partners in the Mochin of ZA, as in the Nekudim; and from there they descend to the NHY of Aba and Ima, and are clothed in them for the need of ZA. Behold, the beginning of the coming out of ZA is in the place of the Keter of Atzilut, namely, in the GAR of Atik. However, Aba and Ima themselves have no root at all in the Keter, but only in the AB alone; and therefore they do not need to receive from the place of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, but from the place of AA, which is the stature of AB. (Item 141).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 234:1
items.html: (To the question) The Makif of the fourth aspect of the Mochin of ZA is a true Makif, which stands in the place of the NHY of Aba and Ima, which is the place of Yeshsut, which are the aspect of the GAR of his Mochin that come from the revealed AB, which he cannot clothe at his birth, because of the clothing of the Mochin in MALZ, as is known. Therefore they surround all the Mochin of ZA. But the Makif of the Tefillin on his forehead is a product of his inner Mochin and a branch of them, except that it is considered a Makif for the aspect of the face, which is from the forehead and below, alone. (Item 144).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 235:1
items.html: (To the question) The matter of the flashing of the Mochin, from which the Makif of the Tefillin came out, operates only in the Daat of the Mochin, which is the aspect of the Lamed, and does not operate in the Hochma and Bina of the Mochin, which are the aspect of the Mem; therefore also its place, from the outside, is likewise opposite the Daat, which is the place of the forehead. (Item 145).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 236:1
items.html: (To the question) The matter of the lights of the Tefillin is born through the flashing of the inner Mochin, whose meaning is the matter of the coupling of the Yesod in the inner Mochin with the Makifim of the upper one. As the Rav says above, in Part 13, (Item 156), that at the time of a favorable moment, the thirteen white [hairs] illuminate in the thirteen hairs, etc., and an illumination is added in the inner Yesod of Atik, and also its light comes out to the outside, etc. Interpretation: through the illumination of the white [hairs] in the hairs, the hairs illuminate in the internality of the Mochin; then the Yesod in the Mochin receives the power to come out to the outside, and from the coupling of the Bina of the Makifim with the Hochma of the Makifim, Bina then bestows its illumination to the internality of the Mochin; and since the internality of the Mochin is corrected in MALZ, they do not contain within themselves this illumination of the Hochma and Bina of the Makifim, and this illumination comes out to the outside, in the aspect of a surrounding light upon the forehead. And in the flashing of the Mochin in AA, this born light is called by the name "forehead of favor," and in ZA it is called "Tefillin." And you see that the Yesod of the inner Mochin cannot come out to the outside, to couple the Bina of the Makifim with the Hochma, except through the illumination of the white [hairs] and the hairs, which illuminate at a favorable moment into the internality of the Mochin. And the reason is, that the aspect of the white [hairs] are the remnants of the revealed AB, which have a grip in the internality of the Mochin; and therefore, when they illuminate in the internality, they arouse the Yesod to draw the illumination of the Makifim. And therefore also in ZA, the aforementioned flashing of the Mochin cannot be, except through the striking of the four white [hairs] and the four hairs of the head in the HaVaYaH of the back of AA, for the white [hairs] and the hairs of the back of the head are the aspect of the NHY of the hairs of the head, and they belong to ZA, which suckles from the NHY of the Galgalta. (Item 149).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 237:1
items.html: (To the question) Since ZA is included in the heads of the shoulders of AA at the time of his pregnancy, through the ascent of the NHY of AA to the HGT, therefore, when the white [hairs] and the hairs illuminate above, in the heads of the shoulders of AA, that illumination reaches the Mochin of ZA. (Item 151).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 238:1
items.html: (To the question) Just as there are in the Mochin of AB, Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura in detail, so they are divided among Aba and Ima and ZA and the Nukva, in their generality: Aba and Ima are the aspect of the Hochma and Bina of the generality; ZA is the aspect of the crown of Hesed of the generality; and the Nukva is the crown of Gevura of the generality. And in this discernment, it is from the aspect of the essentiality alone: that Aba and Ima are the essentiality of Hochma and Bina, ZA is the essentiality of the crown of Hesed, and the Nukva is the essentiality of the crown of Gevura. However, from the aspect of their illumination, even the Nukva has four Mochin — Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura — and therefore ZA, which has the essentiality of the crown of the Hassadim, which is the aspect of the direct light, therefore he has Mochin in the aspect of the passages of the Tefillin. But the Nukva, which has only the essentiality of the Gevura alone, which is only the aspect of Malchut and the returning light, therefore there is in her only the aspects of skin alone, namely, only the aspect of a garment, like the returning light, which is only a garment upon the direct light. Also, Malchut is the aspect of skin, relative to the five garments that clothe one upon the other, called: brain, bone, sinews, flesh, skin. And Malchut is here discerned as skin, for the above reason, being only the aspect of the returning light, which is a garment, like the skin that clothes over the entire Partzuf, from the outside. (Item 160).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 239:1
items.html: One is the permanent state, when it is discerned that his head is very erect, and the beard is raised upward. Its meaning is that his head is erect upward and is completely hidden from the lower ones, for even Aba and Ima have no grip then in his head; and likewise the beard is raised upward, and does not illuminate to Aba and Ima except in the aspect of a Makif from afar. The second state is at the time of the coupling of the kisses, to bring out the Mochin of AB for the sake of Aba and Ima, when it is the ascent of the Partzufim, and the GAR of AA rose to the GAR of Atik, to the stature of Keter; and Aba and Ima, with the throat and HGT of AA, rose to the place of the previous GAR of AA, where is the stature of AB; and the four lower corrections are found to have now risen to the aspect of the head of AA, which is the aspect of AB. However, the eight upper corrections are at the end of the cheeks of the head of AA, which is in the place of Atik; and it is then discerned that the head of AA, with the eight upper corrections, descends from the stature of Keter to the place of Aba and Ima and the four lower corrections, and the coupling is made in the place of the previous mouth of AA, where the mouth of Aba and Ima now clothes; and the eight upper corrections are lowered and illuminate the aspect of the Gime, Yod, Kaf, Kuf in the palate of AA, and the four lower corrections illuminate the aspect of the Alef, He, Het, Ayin in the throat of AA, and upon them the stature of AB comes out for Aba and Ima. And this is discerned as "he bows his head downward and the beard is lowered downward," for the head is lowered to the place of the standing of Aba and Ima, as above, and the beard was lowered to the palate and throat of AA, which is in the place of the mouth of Aba and Ima.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 239:2
items.html: (To the question) The third state is "neither erect nor bowed," and is also called "he bows his head in the aspect of the Mazal VeNakeh alone." And this state is also at the time of the coupling, but for the need of the Mochin of ZA. For the beginning of the Mochin of ZA needs to be from the aspect of the stature of Keter, being that its root is in the Nekudim, from the aspect of the NHY of the Partzuf of the Keter of AK. And therefore the coupling is made in the head of AA, which stands in the place of his ascent, namely, in the GAR of Atik, where is the stature of Keter; and it is found that his head is erect, and he does not bow it downward, to the place of the standing of Aba and Ima, which is in the place of the previous GAR of AA, where is the stature of AB. However, nevertheless, it is impossible to consider him completely erect, because the aspect of the MAN of this coupling is only the MAN of the hairs of the beard, which is the Mazal VeNakeh; and it is found that this stature of AB is much lower than the stature of AB of AA, which is the essentiality of the direct light, and all the more so that it is lower than his stature of Keter; and from this aspect it is discerned that his head is lowered somewhat. For although he does not descend below, but stands in his place in the GAR of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, nevertheless, the coupling is not made from the aspect of his own stature of AA, but from the aspect of the Keter of the AB of the thirty-two paths; and therefore it is impossible to consider him bowed, since he is in his place in the GAR of Atik; and it is impossible to consider him erect, because the coupling is made upon the MAN of the hairs, which is much lower than his own measure. And therefore this is discerned as "he bows his head in the aspect of the Mazal VeNakeh," meaning that there is no true bowing of the head here, but [only] from the fact that the coupling is made upon the MAN of the Mazal VeNakeh. (Item 193).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 240:1
items.html: (To the question) In the bowing of the head of AA, for the need of the coupling of Aba and Ima, he bows his head, and also his beard, to the place of his previous GAR, where is the stature of AB and the standing of Aba and Ima. Not so in the coupling for the need of ZA: there his head is found, in truth, completely erect, for he makes the coupling in the place of the GAR of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda, except that there is here a lowering only from the aspect of the MAN, which are not his MAN but the MAN of the hairs, which is the Mazal VeNakeh. And the reason is explained in the adjacent answer above. (Item 194).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 241:1
items.html: (To the question) The interpretation is that at the time ZA receives his stature through the coupling of AA upon the Mazal of Venakeh, his HGT become the aspect of KHB, and thus the Mochin enlarge his Hesed into the aspect of Hochma, and this Hochma of ZA is called by the name Abraham. (Item 197).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 242:1
items.html: (To the question) The interpretation is that when he attains the stature of his Hochma, the screens in the Yesod of ZA, which are called darkness, being the aspect of Beria, are turned around and become the organ that generates, and through these screens in the Yesod he acquires the power to give birth to the GAR for the souls of the righteous. (Item 198).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 243:1
items.html: (To the question) The Makifim of the Lamed-Mem [of the Tzelem] were never in internal vessels, but rather they are lights that ZA has not yet attained. But the Makifim of the six, of all the aspects, are drawn from the aspect of the returning Makif, which is the aspect of the revealed AB that goes out in the aspect of the internal light at the time of the emergence of the Mochin, at the place of their emergence; only at the time of birth they clothe in the secret of the returning Makif. Thus it is found that those Makifim were already the aspect of the internality of the vessels, and at the time of birth they went out to the outside. (Item 204).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 244:1
items.html: (To the question) It is known that the hairs are the garments of the enveloping light that clothed the returning Makif, at the time it was within the internality of the Mochin, namely at the place of the emergence of the Mochin. And therefore ZA has a returning Makif only from the aspect of the two Atarim alone, because there is his standing and his inclusion at the time of the coupling and the emergence of the Mochin of the revealed AB; and because the GAR were hidden from him at the time of their birth, therefore he has from them a returning Makif, and likewise the hairs, which are their garments. But from the aspect of KHB, ZA has no returning Makif, for he has no share in these Mochin at the place of their emergence, for they went out in the GAR of AA, and the standing of ZA in the Ibur is only at the place of the tops of the shoulders. Therefore he also has no hairs from their aspect. Thus only the hairs of the beard of AA are from the aspect of Hochma, for in it the aspects of KHB of the Mochin went out. But the hairs of the beard of ZA are only from the aspect of Daat, which are the two Atarim drawn from the tops of the shoulders of AA, where he is included at the time of the emergence of the Mochin. And it was already explained above that ZA has KHB and HGT also from the aspect of the tops of the shoulders of AA, except that all these KHB and HGT are called by the name Daat. And only the KHB and HGT that he receives from the aspect of the inheritance of AVI are called the true KHB. (Item 213).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 245:1
items.html: The difference between the hairs of the head and the hairs of the beard is only at the time they are in the aspect of Makifim, for then they too are divided according to the three aspects of the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK. However, at the time of the coupling, when the hairs enter into the internality and serve in the secret of MAN, then the hairs of the head and the hairs of the beard join into a single stature, in which the aspect of the GAR is in the hairs of the head and the aspect of the ZAT is in the hairs of the beard, namely according to their clothing upon the revealed AB. And therefore it is possible to say that the thirteen Tikkunei Dikna of ZA are drawn from the hairs of the head, for being the aspect of the GAR of the hairs, they are considered the principal bestowers. And it is possible to say that the thirteen Tikkunei Dikna of ZA are drawn from the hairs of the beard, because every aspect in the lower one takes from the aspect opposite to it in the upper one; thus the hairs of the head of ZA receive from the hairs of the head of AA, and the hairs of the beard of ZA receive from the hairs of the beard of AA.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 245:2
items.html: (To the question) However, with greater precision, we discern that ZA does not receive his thirteen Tikkunei Dikna except from the thirteen covenants of the lower beard of AA. And this is because the ladder of the degrees never changes, and just as from its beginning ZA clothes only upon the NHY of AA, so too even at the peak of his ascent, namely in the GAR of AA, he does not clothe the GAR of AA literally, but only the NHY of AA alone, for the GAR of AA then ascended higher, namely into the AB of AK, and only the NHY of AA stand then in the place of the former GAR of AA, and ZA again stands in the place of the NHY of AA, as at the beginning of his smallness. And therefore also in the aspect of the hairs, which are divided into the three aspects of the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK like the internal vessels, ZA is found to always clothe and receive only from the aspect of the TZADIK of the hairs, called the lower beard, which stands in the place of the NHY of AA. Except that at the time of the ascent of the NHY of AA to the place of AVI, in his HGT, namely at the Musaf of Shabbat, the lower beard is included of the nine upper Tikkunim, for it is included there in the LAMED of the Tzelem of the aspect of the hairs. And when the NHY of AA ascend to the place of his GAR, namely on Shabbat at Mincha, then the lower beard is included of the thirteen upper Tikkunim, and the lower beard itself is corrected in the aspect of the thirteen covenants, and then ZA receives through it his thirteen Tikkunei Dikna in their fullness. (Item 215, and Item 217, and Item 224).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 246:1
items.html: (To the question) The matter of the MEM of the Tzelem that ZA receives at Mincha of Shabbat, at the time of his ascent to the GAR of AA: its meaning is that same level of the place of the emergence of the Mochin of AB, from their beginning in AVI, for these Mochin are divided into the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK in general, in the manner of the division of the six aspects: one is the place of their emergence in the GAR of AA; two is the NHY of AVI in the place of the HGT of AA; three is the aspect of ZA himself, who is in the NHY of AA. Thus on Shabbat at Mincha ZA ascends to the place of AVI, in which the Mochin emerged at the time of their clothing in the GAR of AA. And therefore, just as AVI did not ascend then beyond the aspect of the four lower Tikkunim, for they stood in the place of the throat and the HGT that became the GAR of AA, which is the place of the four Tikkunim that hang from the throat, but they did not reach the eight upper Tikkunim that hang at the end of the cheeks of the head of AA, for they then ascended to the place of the Reisha de Lo It Yeda — so too it is literally in ZA, who ascends only to the place of that throat and HGT, namely to the four lower Tikkunim, and does not touch at all the eight upper Tikkunim, which are one degree above him. (Item 221).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 247:1
items.html: The beard of AA is divided into three aspects: MEM-LAMED-TZADIK, like the hairs of the head of AA, which are three Havayot and one that includes them all; and they are KHB, HGT, NHY, plus the aspect of Malchut that includes them all, as is known. Now, the essence of ZA is VAK, which are the KHB HGT of the vessels and the HGT NHY of the lights, discerned as the NRNChY of the Nefesh and the NR of the Ruach. And it is known that according to the value of the internal ones, so is the value of the Makifim; therefore he must also have, from the aspect of the hairs of the beard, those same aspects: the NRNChY of the Nefesh and the NR of the Ruach. And it was explained above, in Part 13, in the explanation of the thirteen Tikkunim of AA, that the two Tikkunim of the upper lip — the hairs and the Orcha — are the VAK and GAR of the Ibur, which are the NRNChY of the Nefesh, and are called Rachum and VeChanun. And the two Tikkunim of the lower lip, called Erech [and] Apayim, are the VAK and GAR of the Ruach. See there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 247:2
items.html: And therefore also the beard of ZA draws the aspect of the VAK and GAR of the Nefesh from its corresponding aspect in the beard of AA, namely from the first three Tikkunim, which are El, Rachum and VeChanun, discerned as the Yod-Hey-Vav of the first HaVaYaH of the beard of AA: for Tikkun 1, El, is the root of the beard; and Tikkun Rachum is the VAK of the Nefesh; and Tikkun VeChanun is the GAR of the Nefesh, in the same way that they are discerned in AA himself. Thus from the first three Tikkunim he completes the aspect of the Nefesh of his beard, and they shine in the first three Tikkunim of the beard of ZA, which are Erech, Apayim, and VeRav Chesed.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 247:3
items.html: (To the question) And the aspect of the Ruach the beard of Zeir Anpin draws from the aspect of the Vav-Hey of the second HaVaYaH of the beard of AA, called the HaVaYaH that is behind the shoulders of AA, which is the aspect of Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, and the Ruach of the beard; and it draws only the VAK of the Ruach, which are the Vav-Hey, and not the GAR, for from the aspect of permanence ZA has no GAR of the Ruach. And they are VeEmet and VeNotzer Chesed. For the second HaVaYaH has four Tikkunim: Apayim and VeRav Chesed are the Yod-Hey of the second HaVaYaH, and VeEmet and VeNotzer are the Vav-Hey of the second HaVaYaH. And since ZA must also receive from the Galgalta of AA, for he needs three partners — Keter and AVI — therefore he also receives from the Yod of the lower HaVaYaH, namely the Tikkun LeAlafim, which is from the aspect of the five Tikkunim drawn from the Galgalta of AA. Thus for the aspect of the VAK of his Ruach he receives from the Yod of the lower HaVaYaH, which is drawn from the Galgalta of AA, and from the Vav-Hey of the HaVaYaH of the HGT, as above. However, from these three only two Tikkunim are corrected for him, which are the Vav-Hey of the Ruach, called in ZA VeNosei Avon and VePesha; and these, from the aspect of the Names of HaVaYaH in the beard of ZA, are considered the Yod-Hey of the middle HaVaYaH, for in the vessels it is always discerned that the upper ones are enlarged first, and therefore the VAK of the Ruach are received in the Yod-Hey of the vessels of the Ruach, as is known. And the sixth Tikkun of ZA, which is VeNakeh, receives from the two aspects of the Hey-Tav in the first two Havayot of the thirteen Tikkunim of AA, namely from the Hey-Tav of the first HaVaYaH, and from the Hey-Tav of the HaVaYaH of the HGT. And the reason is explained below. (Items 224 and 225).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 248:1
items.html: (To the question) Because at the time of Gadlut the NHY of the Katnut become the HGT of the Gadlut, and new NHY come to him. And at the time he has only VAK in the beard, namely Nefesh and Ruach, they clothe in the KHB HGT of the vessels of the hairs of the beard: the first three of ZA — Erech, Apayim, and VeRav Chesed — which are the KHB of the vessels, are clothed by the light of the Ruach, and are therefore discerned as HGT. And in the last three — VeNosei Avon, VePesha, and VeNakeh — which are discerned as the vessels of HGT, the light of the Nefesh of the beard clothes in them, and they are therefore discerned as the aspect of NHY. And the Tikkun VeNakeh is now the Yesod of the beard, in which is the terminating screen, which receives from the Hey-Tav in the two Havayot of the beard of AA. And the reason that it needs the two aspects of the Hey-Tav is that at the time it attains the new NHY, to complete for it the nine Tikkunim, then the three Tikkunim VeNosei Avon, VePesha, and VeNakeh, which are now NHY, will then return to be HGT, and the Tikkun VeNakeh will then be the aspect of the chest within the Tifferet; and the screen in the Tikkun VeNakeh will then descend to the new Yesod, called on thirds. And therefore, before it attains the new NHY, it must have in it the two aspects of the Hey-Tav: one, of the aspect of the point of the chest, and two, of the aspect of the point of the Yesod, because afterward, in the Gadlut, it is destined to lower the point of the Yesod that is in it now, to the new Yesod, and it will then remain with the screen of the point of the chest. Thus the Tikkun VeNakeh, at the time that it has only six Tikkunim, is necessarily a bearer of the two points: of the point of the chest and of the point of the Yesod. And therefore it must now receive from the two aspects of the Hey-Tav in the beard of AA, namely from the Hey-Tav of the first HaVaYaH, which is the aspect of the HGT of the beard of ZA, and there is the point of the chest. And it must likewise receive the aspect of the Hey-Tav of the second HaVaYaH of the beard of AA, which are in ZA the aspect of the NHY, and this Hey-Tav is for it the point of the Yesod. Thus the Tikkun VeNakeh, which is now the Yesod, is included of the two points together, of the chest and of the Yesod; and then, when it attains the new NHY, the point of the Yesod descends from the Tikkun VeNakeh to the Tikkun of on thirds, and the point of the chest remains in the Tikkun VeNakeh. (Item 226).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Topics 249:1
items.html: (To the question) Because when it is spoken of the drawing of the lights, it is a necessity that he receives from the Vav-Hey of the HaVaYaH that is behind the shoulders, which is the name of HGT and Ruach; and he does not receive from the Yod-Hey of the Ruach that is there, but rather from the Vav-Hey of this HaVaYaH, which is the Nefesh-Ruach of the Ruach. However, from the aspect of the Names in ZA himself, which are the aspect of the vessels, behold the VAK of the lights clothe in the GAR of the vessels, and thus the Nefesh-Ruach of the Ruach, which clothe in the Yod-Hey of the HaVaYaH, are found. This is known by the inverse relation that exists between the vessels and the lights. It is also known that the letters of the HaVaYaH hint at the vessels. And accordingly it is found that in AA himself, who already has also the GAR of the Ruach, the GAR clothe in the Yod-Hey, and the VAK in the Vav-Hey. But in ZA, who does not yet have the GAR of the Ruach, the VAK of the Ruach clothe in the GAR of the vessels, which are the Yod-Hey. (Item 268).
